column1: # Capitalisation rulings — the cards corpus:casefix cannot decide by rule.
# German capitalises nouns and nothing else, but "is this a noun" is not something
# a script can read off a card whose `pos` is empty, and a capital is sometimes
# correct on a word that isn't one (polite "Ihr", "Verzeihung!" as an exclamation).
# So each of these is a decision, recorded with its reason and applied by casefix.
#   lowercase  detail = the pos to set    lowercase the headword, rebuild the id
#   noun       detail = "der Xxx|die Xxx" it was a noun all along: set pos, article,
#   drop       detail = surviving id      duplicate of a card that is already correct
#   keep       detail = pos               the capital is right; here is why
# ── Pronouns. German writes every one of these lowercase. The polite forms (Sie,
#    Ihnen, Ihr) are capitalised, but each card here is glossed with its ordinary
#    sense, so the ordinary spelling is the one to teach.
